name: When transaction value is rejected — the ordered cascade into the valuation Rules
definition: Section 15(4) says that where the value cannot be determined under s.15(1), it shall be determined in such manner as may be prescribed. Section 15(5) goes further: for supplies notified by the Government on the recommendations of the Council, the prescribed manner applies NOTWITHSTANDING s.15(1) and s.15(4). The prescribed manner is Chapter IV of the CGST Rules, and it is an ORDERED cascade, not a menu. Rule 27 governs consideration not wholly in money; rule 28 governs distinct or related persons other than through an agent; rule 29 governs goods supplied through an agent; rule 30 values at one hundred and ten percent of cost where no preceding rule of the Chapter determines the value; rule 31 is the residual, available only where rules 27 to 30 cannot determine it. Rules 31A and 32 open with a non obstante clause over the Chapter for the supplies they name.
why_it_exists: A rejected transaction value must still produce a number, and the number must be reproducible by anyone auditing it. The cascade does that by fixing the ORDER: each rule names the rules it falls back to and the order in which they apply. An engine that picks whichever rule yields a convenient figure produces a defensible-looking value that no second party can reproduce — which is indistinguishable from an invented one.
inputs: which s.15(1) condition failed — relatedness, or sole consideration, or both
whether the supply is between distinct or related persons (s.25(4), s.25(5), the s.15 Explanation)
whether the supply is made through an agent
whether the supply is one notified under s.15(5)
whether the supply is one named in rule 31A or rule 32
for rule 30: the cost of production or manufacture, the cost of acquisition, or the cost of provision
outputs: the position in the cascade at which the value was determined
the value, or an explicit failure naming the input that could not be obtained
preconditions: s.15(1) has been tested and does not apply (GST-VAL-TRANSACTION-VALUE), or s.15(5) applies notwithstanding it
the supply has been classified as goods or services, since rule 31's proviso is available only for services
rules: UNKNOWN — no atomic rule has been written into Rule_Library for the ordering of rules 27 to 31; Rule_Library was not modified by this record
exceptions: rule 31A opens 'Notwithstanding anything contained in the provisions of this Chapter' for lottery, betting, gambling and horse racing — it displaces the cascade for those supplies
rule 32 opens with the same non obstante clause but the special valuations it carries are AT THE OPTION OF THE SUPPLIER, not mandatory
rule 31, proviso — for a supply of services the supplier may opt for the residual rule, ignoring rule 30; the option exists for services only

common_mistakes: treating rules 27 to 31 as alternatives and selecting the most convenient — each rule states the rule it falls back to and the order
reaching rule 30 or rule 31 without first showing that every preceding rule of the Chapter failed
applying rule 30's one hundred and ten percent to a supply where rule 28 or rule 29 could have produced a value
using the rule 31 proviso for a supply of goods — the proviso names supply of services only
assuming that satisfying both s.15(1) conditions ends the enquiry — s.15(5) overrides s.15(1) for notified supplies
computing a value under the Rules and then forgetting the s.15(2) additions still apply to the supply

evidence_required: the determination that s.15(1) does not apply, and which condition failed
the facts that select the governing rule — relatedness, distinctness, agency, or non-money consideration
for rule 30: the costing records supporting cost of production, manufacture, acquisition or provision
for rule 31: a written record of why rules 27 to 30 could not determine the value, and of the reasonable means used
confidence_factors: zero where the failed s.15(1) condition has not been identified, because the condition that failed selects the rule
weak at rule 31 by construction — 'reasonable means' is not a computation, and two competent people can reach two numbers
weak wherever open market value is asserted without evidence of an actual comparable supply (GST-VAL-OPEN-MARKET)
UNKNOWN for s.15(5) — the notification listing those supplies is not held locally, so a supply cannot be cleared of being inside it
validation_checks: the governing rule is named explicitly, never implied by the arithmetic used
where rule 30 or rule 31 was used, the failure of every preceding rule of the Chapter is recorded
the rule 31 proviso is used only for a supply of services
the s.15(2) additions have been applied to a value determined under the Rules, not only to a transaction value
a value that cannot be determined is reported as undetermined — never completed with an estimate
examples: a supply for consideration not wholly in money where the open market value is available — rule 27(a) determines the value and the cascade stops there
counterexamples: valuing a related-party supply at one hundred and ten percent of cost under rule 30 without first testing rule 28's open market value and like kind and quality limbs — the cascade was entered out of order
a supplier of goods electing the rule 31 residual method to avoid rule 30 — the proviso permits that only for a supply of services

evidence.quote: Where the value of the supply of goods or services or both cannot be determined under sub-section (1), the same shall be determined in such manner as may be prescribed.

Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1) or sub-section (4), the value of such supplies as may be notified by the Government on the recommendations of the Council shall be determined in such manner as may be prescribed.

if the value is not determinable under clause (a) or clause (b) or clause (c), be the sum total of consideration in money and such further amount in money that is equivalent to consideration not in money as determined by the application of rule 30 or rule 31 in that order.
if the value is not determinable under clause (a) or (b), be the value as determined by the application of rule 30 or rule 31, in that order:

Where the value of a supply of goods or services or both is not determinable by any of the preceding rules of this Chapter, the value shall be one hundred and ten percent of the cost of production or manufacture or the cost of acquisition of such goods or the cost of provision of such services.

Where the value of supply of goods or services or both cannot be determined under rules 27 to 30, the same shall be determined using reasonable means consistent with the principles and the general provisions of section 15 and the provisions of this Chapter:
Provided that in the case of supply of services, the supplier may opt for this rule, ignoring rule 30.
Notwithstanding anything contained in the provisions of this Chapter, the value in respect of supplies specified below shall be determined in the manner provided hereinafter.

Notwithstanding anything contained in the provisions of this Chapter, the value in respect of supplies specified below shall, at the option of the supplier, be determined in the manner provided hereinafter.
